title: Console aggregation-window lag causing missing timeseries and orphaned spans
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple production incidents across Hosted and Dedicated tenants surfaced missing time-series in Console dashboards and a surge of orphaned spans in tracing during regional overloads (2026-03-04 through 2026-03-06). Root cause investigation shows an aggregation-window lag and shard checkpoint desynchronization in the telemetry ingestion pipeline. The aggregator was aggressively evicting partial shard windows when downstream acknowledgement was delayed, which caused metrics to be dropped from the live tile window and left spans unstitched in the trace index. Several enterprise customers escalated (SLO dashboards blanking for 10-30m and tracing gaps affecting root-cause analysis). This ticket tracks the production bugfix, short-term mitigations, and post-incident recovery/backfill plan.
impact_summary: Affected tenants (hosted and dedicated pools) experienced intermittent dashboard blanking and missing metric points during peak traffic, with a correlated increase in orphaned spans in APM. Customer escalations: 4 enterprise tenants reported SLO graphs disappearing; 2 customers opened high-severity support cases. Estimated user-facing downtime of metric visibility: 10-30 minutes per incident window. Business risk: high — impaired incident investigation and SLA confidence.

root_cause: Aggregator eviction policy used a conservative memory reclaim heuristic tied to a per-shard STAMP that was updated only when the downstream index acknowledged a complete window. Under transient downstream latency the shard STAMP did not advance, the aggregator considered those windows stale and evicted partial aggregates. That eviction deleted metric points from the live window and dropped span attachments that hadn't been indexed yet, resulting in missing tiles and orphaned spans. Watermark propagation between ingestion proxies and aggregator nodes was unreliable during region spikes, increasing the likelihood of the race.
short_term_mitigation: Increased aggregator in-memory retention window from 60s to 180s for affected clusters to prevent premature eviction
Paused automatic aggressive eviction in cluster autoscaling during incident windows via feature-flag (ff:agg_safe_retention)
Kicked off on-demand backfill jobs for top 5 affected tenants (re-ingest from persistence with preserved event timestamps)
Notified impacted customers and provided temporary dashboard snapshots and CSV exports
long_term_fix_plan: Add a 'window-safe' eviction marker: only evict windows where downstream index reports explicit checkpoint advancement or when TTL is exceeded by >2x expected lateness
Improve watermark propagation: propagate shard frontier updates in a compacted heartbeat at ingestion proxy to guarantee delivery within 5s under load
Backfill tooling: build incremental backfill pipeline that can rehydrate live windows without overwriting newer data and that tracks customer-scoped reinstatement progress
Span stitching: update span index to record pre-indexed references to allow late arrivals to be attached rather than dropped
E2E automated test: replay harness for injection of ingress latency and verify no tile blanking across 72h simulated load
acceptance_criteria: Aggregation eviction logic no longer drops metric points for late-arriving data within configured lateness (default 2m)
Live dashboard blanking rate for canary tenants is <0.2% during 24h smoke test under synthetic delay injection
Span orphan rate (spans without parent/trace id attachment) reduced to <0.5% in production after rollout
Backfill job completes for 100% of affected customers listed in the incident and dashboards reflect restored points
Postmortem published and customer communication sent to all impacted customers
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate ingestion proxy latency spike (delay ACKs to aggregator by 90-120s) while sending high-cardinality metrics
Observe aggregator eviction logs: search for 'evicting-window' events where shard_stamp < downstream_stamp
Replay same events from persistence into backfill pipeline and verify live panel shows restored points
Send a set of spans with delayed indexing (50-120s) and confirm that span stitching attaches late spans after code change

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increasing retention window increases memory pressure on aggregator nodes. Mitigation: feature-flag via ff:agg_safe_retention and autoscale to add headroom during retention extension
Risk: Backfill may cause data duplication or conflict with newer points. Mitigation: backfill pipeline writes with idempotent merge by timestamp and uses merge-window semantics
Risk: Rollout could expose unrelated aggregator bugs under new code paths. Mitigation: staged canary rollout with telemetry guardrails and automatic rollback on alert
